whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the B2C Commerce Developer exam for?

personas.label: SFCC developers
personas.description: You build and customize B2C Commerce storefronts using SFRA, ISML, and server-side JavaScript and want the certification to validate your full-stack SFCC skills.

personas.label: Full-stack commerce engineers
personas.description: You work with controllers, templates, OCAPI/SCAPI, and Business Manager configuration and need a credential that covers the entire SFCC development stack.

personas.label: Technical leads
personas.description: You manage cartridge architecture, deployment pipelines, and storefront performance for B2C Commerce projects and want to formalize your technical leadership.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the B2C Commerce Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The B2C Commerce Developer exam is considered one of the harder Salesforce developer certifications. The ~65% passing score is moderate, but the exam covers the full SFCC stack — from SFRA architecture and ISML templates to OCAPI/SCAPI integration and Business Manager configuration — demanding broad and deep hands-on experience.
bullets: ~65% passing score — moderate on paper, but the breadth of topics (SFRA, scripting, APIs, data model, deployment) makes it demanding.
Full-stack depth — questions span server-side controllers, ISML templates, client-side JavaScript, and Business Manager operations, so you cannot skip any layer.
Hands-on SFRA experience essential — real project experience with SFRA controller development and at least one OCAPI or SCAPI integration is the strongest preparation.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Spend time in a B2C Commerce sandbox building custom controllers, overriding SFRA templates, and configuring jobs in Business Manager before booking the exam.

examFormat.heading: B2C Commerce Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Around 40-50% of questions are scenario-based. Common patterns describe a storefront customization requirement and ask which SFRA pattern, controller method, or API approach meets it. Expect questions on cartridge path resolution, template overrides, and OCAPI resource configuration.
bestWayToPass: Master the cartridge override pattern: Know how the cartridge path resolves controllers and templates, and when to use server.extend vs. server.replace.
Build with SFRA hands-on: Create custom controllers, override ISML templates, and work with the dw.* API in a sandbox environment.
Study OCAPI and SCAPI: Understand the Shop API vs. Data API, how authentication works for headless scenarios, and when to use each API.
Know Business Manager inside out: Practice configuring site preferences, running jobs, managing code versions, and diagnosing issues using the request log and pipeline profiler.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers full-stack SFCC development — SFRA cartridge architecture, ISML templates, controller scripting, OCAPI/SCAPI integration, and Business Manager configuration.

keyConcepts.h2: B2C Commerce Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: SFRA Architecture: Cartridges & Override Pattern
blocks.body: **SFRA** is the Salesforce B2C Commerce reference architecture built on a cartridge system. **cartridges** are modular packages containing controllers, templates, models, and static assets. The cartridge path (configured in **Business Manager**) defines override priority — the leftmost cartridge wins. To customize, create a custom cartridge that overrides specific controllers or templates without editing base cartridges. This keeps base cartridge upgrades non-destructive. The `server.extend` and `server.replace` patterns in controllers allow adding before/after steps or completely replacing a route. The developer exam tests the correct use of the override pattern and common mistakes that break cartridge path resolution.

blocks.heading: Controllers, Scripts & Server-Side Logic
blocks.body: **SFRA** controllers are JavaScript modules using the `server` framework. Routes handle GET and POST requests and render templates or return JSON. Middleware functions (authentication, CSRF, consent) can be prepended to any route. Models and helpers contain business logic separated from controllers. `dw.system`, `dw.order`, `dw.catalog` — the Digital SDK — provides access to Commerce Cloud server-side APIs. Custom scripts (`.js` files in `cartridge/scripts/`) encapsulate reusable logic. The exam tests how to add a middleware step to an existing controller route, how to call a custom script from a controller, and common governor limit considerations in server-side scripts.

blocks.heading: Templates (ISML) & Client-Side Assets
blocks.body: ISML (Internet Store Markup Language) is the server-side templating language. `<isinclude>` embeds sub-templates. `<isloop>` iterates collections. `<isset>` assigns variables. `<isif>` handles conditionals. Resource bundles (properties files) provide localized strings. Static assets (JS, CSS, images) are organized in `cartridge/static/` and referenced via `URLUtils.staticURL()`. Webpack compiles and bundles client-side JS in **SFRA**. SASS is compiled to CSS. Client-side JavaScript uses jQuery and Bootstrap in SFRA. The exam tests ISML syntax, how to pass data from controller to template via `pdict`, and how to add a new client-side component.

blocks.heading: Jobs, Feeds & Business Manager Configuration
blocks.body: Commerce Cloud Jobs run server-side scripts on a schedule or on-demand. Jobs process product feeds (import/export), order exports, and inventory updates. The Job Framework uses steps configured in **Business Manager**. IMPEX (Import/Export) handles large data loads via XML or CSV files placed in the IMPEX directory. Site Preferences store admin-configurable settings accessible in code via `dw.system.Site.current.preferences`. Custom Attributes extend standard objects (products, orders, customers) in Business Manager. The exam tests Job configuration, IMPEX file formats, and how to read custom site preferences in controller logic.

blocks.heading: Testing, Debugging & Deployment
blocks.body: Commerce Cloud development uses the `sgmf-scripts` (**SFRA** build tools) and Salesforce Commerce Cloud CLI (`sfcc-ci`) for deployment. Code deployment uploads **cartridges** to a code version, which is then activated. The Request Log and Custom Log APIs (`dw.system.Logger`) support debugging. The Pipeline Profiler identifies slow controller routes. Functional tests use `mochawesome` reports. Unit testing is done with jest and `dw-api-types` mocks for Digital SDK. The exam tests the deployment sequence (cartridge upload → code version activation), how to write a testable controller with mocked dependencies, and how to diagnose errors using **Business Manager** logs.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce B2C Commerce Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The B2C Commerce Developer exam tests hands-on SFCC development: ISML templates, controller development (SFRA), and script development. Focus on the SFRA architecture and how to implement common storefront customizations.

blocks.heading: SFRA Architecture
blocks.body: Know the **storefront** Reference Architecture (**SFRA**) MVC pattern: Routes (controllers), Models (data layer), Templates (ISML views), and how **cartridges** layer on top of SFRA using the cartridge path.

blocks.heading: Controller Development
blocks.body: Know how to create custom routes (server.get/post/append/prepend/replace), use middleware for authentication/CSRF protection, and how to return JSON responses or render ISML templates from controllers.

blocks.heading: ISML Templates
blocks.body: Know ISML syntax: <isset>, <isif>, <isloop>, <isinclude>, <isreplace>, and how to use locale, currency, and content asset tags. Understand how template caching affects dynamic content rendering.

blocks.heading: Script Development
blocks.body: Know how to write CommonJS-style scripts in SFCC, use the dw.* API (dw.catalog, dw.order, dw.customer), and how to call web services from scripts using the dw.net.HTTPClient.

blocks.heading: Business Manager Configuration
blocks.body: Know key **Business Manager** configurations: catalog setup, pricebook management, promotion configuration, **storefront** configuration (site preferences), and how to use the UX Studio for cartridge management.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After Developer
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this certification, common next steps in the developer track:

sampleQuestions.question: What does SFRA stand for in B2C Commerce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Storefront Reference Architecture (SFRA) is the standard reference implementation for B2C Commerce storefronts.

sampleQuestions.question: Which API is used for headless or custom front-end integrations with B2C Commerce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OCAPI/SCAPI (Shop API) is used for headless and custom integrations with B2C Commerce.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a cartridge in B2C Commerce?
options: A modular unit of code that extends storefront functionality
sampleQuestions.explanation: Cartridges contain scripts, templates, and assets that extend or customize the storefront.

sampleQuestions.question: Which scripting language is primarily used in B2C Commerce storefront development?
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2C Commerce uses JavaScript (Node.js) and ISML (template language) for storefront logic and rendering.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the Business Manager in B2C Commerce?
options: To manage catalogs, campaigns, and storefront settings
sampleQuestions.explanation: Business Manager is the admin console for managing B2C Commerce sites, catalogs, and operations.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a pipeline in B2C Commerce?
options: A server-side script that processes a request through sequential steps
sampleQuestions.explanation: Pipelines process requests through sequential script steps.

sampleQuestions.question: Which B2C Commerce template language renders HTML?
sampleQuestions.explanation: ISML is the template language for B2C Commerce storefronts.

sampleQuestions.question: What does OCAPI support?
options: Headless commerce, custom storefronts, and mobile apps
sampleQuestions.explanation: OCAPI enables headless and custom storefront development.

sampleQuestions.question: Which B2C Commerce object represents a product?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Product and Product Variant represent catalog items.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a custom cartridge?
options: To extend or override storefront functionality
sampleQuestions.explanation: Custom cartridges extend or override storefront behavior.

sampleQuestions.question: Which B2C Commerce feature supports A/B testing?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Business Manager supports experiments for A/B testing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Script Debugger support?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Script Debugger supports breakpoints and variable inspection.

sampleQuestions.question: Which deployment method is used for B2C Commerce code?
options: Code deployment via Business Manager or CI/CD
sampleQuestions.explanation: Code deploys via Business Manager or CI/CD pipelines.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the hook mechanism in B2C Commerce?
options: To extend or override pipeline behavior without modifying base code
sampleQuestions.explanation: Hooks allow extension without modifying base cartridges.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice applies to B2C Commerce performance?
options: Use caching, optimize ISML, and minimize API calls
sampleQuestions.explanation: Caching and optimization support storefront performance.
